patch_description: The current pipeline runs SLSQP once from a crude lattice seed, repairs (shrinking radii), then applies COBYLA to every candidate — costing 51s eval time with no score gain (both runs at 2.61). The recommended edit implements the "polish pass": after repair, restart SLSQP from the feasible repaired (centers, radii). Since this warm start is already feasible and near a local optimum with many active tangency constraints, SLSQP can make the fine tangency adjustments (growing radii against walls and neighbors) that the crude seed cannot reach — the most direct route toward closing the gap to 2.635. We apply a second (and third) polish round while it keeps improving. Additionally, we only run the expensive COBYLA stage on the single best refined candidate, cutting runtime dramatically while keeping the score.
